Fields.Label: Subject Identifier
Fields.Description: The subjectid is a unique identifier assigned to each participant in a clinical study. It serves as a key to the tracking of participant information across multiple visits, treatments, and assessments over the course of the study. The format can vary depending on the study protocol, but it typically includes alphanumeric characters. Each subject can be consistently referenced across various datasets and reports, and it helps to maintain the standards for reporting and data management in clinical research.
Fields.Comment: The subjectid variable uniquely identifies each subject enrolled and This variable is used throughout the study to reference and track data related to individual subject, such as their demographic information, clinical data, lab results, and treatment responses

Fields.Label: Study Identifier
Fields.Description: The studyid is a unique identifier assigned to a specific clinical study and is also often called protocol ID. It serves as a reference code that distinguishes one study from another within a research database.Researchers use the studyid to pull together all relevant information about a study, including protocols, participant data, and outcomes.It is essential for reporting results to regulatory agencies, ensuring that all findings are correctly attributed to the right study.
Fields.Comment: Identifier for the specific study being conducted and This variable is used to reference and track data related to individual studies, such as subject data, clinical outcomes, and research findings

Fields.Label: Days on Treatment
Fields.Description: Study days or Days on Treatment is the total time the subject has been on the study.
Fields.Comment: Number of days into the study at which the observation was taken.This measure helps to standardize timelines and schedules for data collection, assessments across all subjects.

Fields.Label: Age
Fields.Description: The age variable indicates the age of a subject at the time of their enrollment in the clinical study. It is typically measured in years but can also be presented in months or days for younger subjects.It is a critical demographic variable that helps categorize participants and assess how age influences treatment outcomes and Understanding how age affects treatment efficacy and safety supports the move towards more personalized treatment approaches.The age is usually represented as a numeric value
Fields.Comment: N/A

Fields.Label: Disease
Fields.Description: The disease variable indicates the specific disease stage that a subject is diagnosed with at the time of enrollment in the clinical study and helps in categorizing subjects based on their disease stage, which is essential for studies focused on specific disease stages. Ensures that the study addresses specific health needs, allowing for targeted research that can lead to better therapies. This variable is typically a categorical text field that describes the disease
Fields.Comment: The medical condition or disease being studied and the clinical stage of the disease that the subject is diagnosed with at the time of enrollment

Fields.Label: Gender
Fields.Description: The gender variable indicates the sex of the participant in a clinical study. It is typically categorized as male, female, or other classifications depending on the studys inclusivity.It requires gender-specific data to assess the safety and efficacy of treatments across different demographic groups and supports the analysis of treatment effects and safety profiles, helping to ensure that medical interventions are effective and appropriate for all genders.
Fields.Comment: The biological sex of the subject, typically categorized as male or female and This variable is essential for demographic analysis, understanding gender-specific responses to treatment, and ensuring the study findings are applicable to different gender groups.

Fields.Label: Overall Survival (OS) Time
Fields.Description: Overall survival (OS) refers to the duration of time from the start of treatment (or the diagnosis of disease) until death from any cause. OS is used to measure the effectiveness of a treatment in extending the life of subjects with a specific disease, particularly cancer, and it helps in evaluating and comparing the efficacy of different therapies. OS is typically expressed in units of time, such as months or years. For example, an OS of 18.2 months indicates that, on average, subjects lived for that duration after starting treatment.
Fields.Comment: Overall survival, representing the duration of time from either the date of diagnosis or the start of treatment for a disease until the death of the patient from any cause

Fields.Label: Overall Survival (OS) Event Indicator
Fields.Description: The OS Ind is an indicator that typically represents the status of a participant’s overall survival in a clinical study. It is essential for evaluating the effectiveness of new treatments in prolonging life and improving patient outcomes and helps researchers quickly determine the survival status of participants without needing to review detailed records.The OS Ind is usually a binary variable.[1: Indicates that the subject is alive (alive status).],[0: Indicates that the subject has died (deceased status).]
Fields.Comment: Overall survival indicator, a binary variable indicating at a certain time point

Fields.Label: Response Status
Fields.Description: ORRNRIA typically refers to the object response status to treatment for the subject in the context of clinical trials.
Fields.Comment: The orrnria variable may stands for Objective Response Rate (ORR) Indicator, which classifies subjects into responders or non-responders based on their clinical response to treatment. It may be used to to categorize and analyze the treatment response or indicate the response status of a patient

Fields.Label: Response Category
Fields.Description: The OR Inv variable refers to the overall response to treatment in a clinical study, indicating the response status of a subject based on specific criteria. It is often used to summarize how well a treatment has worked for a subject.Researchers analyze OR Inv data to evaluate treatment outcomes and determine the proportion of subjects who respond positively to therapy.This information can be crucial for comparing different treatment regimens in clinical trials.The format may vary by study but typically uses categorical labels. Common categories include: [CR: Complete Response],[PR: Partial Response],[SD: Stable Disease],[PD: Progressive Disease]
Fields.Comment: It may stands for Overall Response by Investigator. It indicates the clinical response of a subject to treatment as assessed by the investigator

Fields.Label: Progression-Free Survival (PFS) Time
Fields.Description: Progression-Free Survival (PFS) is a measure of the length of time during and after treatment in which a subjects disease does not worsen . It is a key endpoint in clinical study. It provides information on how long patients can expect to maintain their current health status while undergoing treatment and expressed in time units, such as months or years. For example, a PFS of 2.5 months indicates that, on average, patients experienced no disease progression for that duration after starting treatment.
Fields.Comment: Progression Free Survival(PFS), a measure of the length of time during and after the treatment of a disease and it used to assess and compare the effectiveness of treatments in delaying disease progression.

Fields.Label: Progression-Free Survival (PFS) Event Indicator
Fields.Description: The pfs_ind variable indicates whether or not the patient has experienced disease progression during the study. When analyzing PFS data, clinicians and researchers look at the proportion of patients who have a pfs_ind of 0 versus 1. A higher proportion of patients with pfs_ind = 0 suggests that the treatment is effective in prolonging the time before the disease progresses.
Fields.Comment: Progression Free Survival indicator,it may indicates whether a progression-free survival (PFS) event has occurred for each subject and This binary variable distinguishes between subjects who have experienced disease progression or event and those who have not.

Fields.Label: Region
Fields.Description: Region refers to a specific geographical area where the participant participates in the study at the site. This can encompass continents, countries, or more localized areas. Researchers can compare treatment outcomes across different regions to identify trends, effectiveness, or potential adverse events linked to regional factors. During statistical analysis, data can be stratified by region to assess whether certain treatments work better in specific populations.
Fields.Comment: The geographical region where the study is being conducted or where the participating sites are located and understanding potential regional variations in patient demographics, disease characteristics, and treatment practices

Fields.Label: Therapy
Fields.Description: Therapy indicates whether the subject has received treatment prior to entering the clinical trial. It is important to understand potential interactions with prior medications as compared to the treatment as part of the clinical trial.
Fields.Comment: Typically denotes whether the subject received prior medical treatment

Fields.Label: Treatment Group
Fields.Description: The treatment group categorizes subjects based on the specific treatment or intervention they receive during the study. This categorization is crucial for comparing outcomes across different therapies. Treatment groups are essential for statistical analyses, including hypothesis testing and estimating treatment effects. Is indicated as Monotherapy. This means that the participant is part of a group receiving a single treatment without combination with other therapies. Understanding this helps in analyzing how this particular treatment affects the subjects outcomes compared to those in other treatment groups.
Fields.Comment: Treatment group, indicating which group the participant belongs to in terms of the treatment received and it help in comparing outcomes between different treatment groups and assessing the efficacy and safety of each treatment approach

Fields.Label: Enrollment Dose
Fields.Description: Dose refers to the quantity of a drug or treatment that a subject receives during the clinical study. This indicates that each participant in the study receives this specific quantity of the treatment. Understanding the context of this dose is crucial for analyzing its impact on outcomes like overall survival, progression-free survival, and adverse events. It helps healthcare providers determine how to prescribe treatments effectively and safely to study.
Fields.Comment: The dosage or dose of a treatment administered to subject and quantifies the amount of medication, radiation, or other interventions received by each subject.

Fields.Label: Adverse Events (AE) Indicator
Fields.Description: Adverse events (AEs) are any undesirable experiences or side effects that occur during or after the administration of a treatment in a clinical study. If the entry for adv_event is noted as No. This indicates that the subject did not experience any significant adverse events during the study period, suggesting a favorable safety profile for the treatment.Monitoring adverse events helps ensure patient safety, informs regulatory decisions, and contributes to the overall understanding of a treatments risk-benefit
Fields.Comment: Adverse events experienced by subjects during the study

Fields.Label: Sample Identifier
Fields.Description: Sample ID is a unique alphanumeric code that helps track and identify individual biological samples collected during the study. This may include samples of blood, tissue, or other biological materials.The sample ID ensures accurate tracking and organization of samples throughout the study. It prevents mix-ups and allows researchers to easily reference specific samples during analysis.
Fields.Comment: The sampleid variable uniquely identifies each biological sample collected from subjects and ensures that each sample can be accurately tracked, stored, and analyzed

Fields.Label: Visit (char)
Fields.Description: visitc indicates the sequence or order of scheduled visits that participants have in the clinical study. Each visit represents a point in time when the subject is assessed, receives treatment, or undergoes procedures related to the study. Here, the visitc is recorded as C1D1. This likely indicates that this data pertains to the first cycle (C1) of treatment, Day 1 (D1). This specificity is crucial for understanding the timing of the data in relation to the treatment.
Fields.Comment: Visit code or identifier (char)

Fields.Label: Visit (numeric)
Fields.Description: Visit Number (visitn) indicates the expected nominal day of the visit that a subject attends during the clinical study.The visitn helps in monitoring a participants progression through the study timeline. By knowing the visit number, researchers can easily reference which visit the data corresponds to in relation to treatment cycles. Hence, the visitn variable is expected nominal day of visitc variable.
Fields.Comment: Visit code or identifier (numeric)

Fields.Label: Timepoint (char)
Fields.Description: The timec variable  indicates the timepoint of the assessment wihtin a given visit. This can help researchers understand the timing of data collection in relation to treatment cycles. Monitoring the timing of assessment within visits ensures that subjects are following the study protocol correctly. Here, timec is recorded as PreD, which likely indicates that the assessment took place prior to treatment (e.g., a baseline measurement within the cycle).
Fields.Comment: Timepoint of assessment within the visit (char)

Fields.Label: Visit+TimePoint Code
Fields.Description: The visittimec variable indicates the exact timing of a visit in relation to treatment cycles or specific time points, providing more detailed information than just the visit number or cycle. Here, the visittimec is noted as C1D1-PreD. This likely indicates that the visit took place on the first cycle (C1), Day 1 (D1), specifically prior to the treatment administration (PreD). This context is crucial for understanding the timing of baseline measurements relative to the treatment.
Fields.Comment: Combained visit and time point (char)

Fields.Label: Control Indicator
Fields.Description: The control indicator functions as a flag that serves as a universal control for samples intended for visualization. Only those samples marked with a control flag of zero are included in the biomarker analysis. If a replicate or undesirable sample needs to be marked, it is assigned a value of one; such samples are regarded as masked with a flag of one.
Fields.Comment: Indicator variable the  control

Fields.Label: Panel
Fields.Description: A panel represents a group of related assessments or laboratory tests that are performed on the subject at specified time points during the clinical study. This can include various biomarkers, laboratory analyses, or clinical evaluations.It allows for systematic collection of data related to multiple aspects of subject health or disease status, providing a holistic view of treatment effects.
Fields.Comment: Indicates the biomarker panel being analyzed it may be a set of biomarkers, genes, or molecular targets analyzed as part of a diagnostic or research assay

Fields.Label: Batch
Fields.Description: Batch Number is a unique identifier that designates a collection of biological samples that were collected, stored, or processed together. This number helps to track and manage samples during laboratory analysis. It helps ensure quality control by allowing laboratories to monitor and verify that all samples within a batch For example, all samples collected on the same day or processed in the same run could share the same batch number.
Fields.Comment: Batch number or identifier for sample processed together  anf it used to group samples, assays, or experiments that were processed together under similar conditions

Fields.Label: Quality Control Result
Fields.Description: Quality Control (QC) implemented to ensure that the data and samples collected during the study meet predefined standards of quality and accuracy. Here,  the qc variable is noted as PASS, indicating that the sample or data associated with this entry met all quality control criteria and is considered acceptable for analysis.
Fields.Comment: Indicates the quality control status of the sample

Fields.Label: Quality Control Comment
Fields.Description: QC Comment allows researchers to document specific observations, issues, or notes regarding the quality control checks performed on samples or data. Keeping thorough QC comments is crucial for maintaining high standards of research quality.
Fields.Comment: Comments related to Quality control assessments

Fields.Label: Biomarker Type
Fields.Description: Biomarker Type indicates the specific kind of biological marker being measured or analyzed. Biomarkers can be substances or processes that indicate a particular disease state or response to treatment, and Understanding the type of biomarker is critical for clinicians when considering diagnostic or prognostic implications and for guiding treatment decisions based on biomarker profiles.
Fields.Comment: The biomarker_type variable identifies the specific types or methods of biomarkers being analyzed in a clinical trial. This helps classify biomarkers based on the technology or methodology used to measure them, which is critical for understanding

Fields.Label: Sample Type
Fields.Description: Sample Type indicates the nature of the biological material collected for analysis, which could include various forms such as blood or plasma.Different sample types require specific processing methods and analytical techniques. For example, plasma samples may be analyzed for circulating biomarkers, while blood samples may be examined for flowcytometry analysis.
Fields.Comment: The variable describes the kind of biological material collected from subjects and as different sample types may require different handling procedures and can yield different types of data.

Fields.Label: Lab Processing Date
Fields.Description: Laboratory Date indicates the specific date when the sample was processed or analyzed in the laboratory. This date is crucial for tracking the timing of laboratory assessments. It helps establish a timeline for when samples were analyzed, allowing researchers to correlate laboratory results with clinical events
Fields.Comment: Records the date on which a sample was collected or processed in the laboratory

Fields.Label: Collection Date
Fields.Description: Collection Date indicates the specific date when the biological sample was obtained from the participant. This is a critical piece of information for tracking the timeline of sample and it helps create a timeline for when samples were collected, which is essential for correlating laboratory results with clinical events
Fields.Comment: Date when the sample was collected from the subject

Fields.Label: Collection Time
Fields.Description: Collection Time indicates the specific time at which the biological sample was obtained from the subjects. This time point is crucial for understanding the conditions under which the sample was collected. It  provides precise information about when the sample was taken, which is important for analyzing the dynamics of biological markers
Fields.Comment: Time when the sample was collected from the subject

Fields.Label: DB Table Identifier
Fields.Description: Table ID serves as a reference to a particular dataset that contains related information or data points within the  study. This helps organize and manage the data systematically. It helps categorize and organize data effectively, making it easier for researchers to locate and retrieve specific information related to the study. The tableid would likely correspond to a specific table that contains detailed information about the samples, visits, or other relevant variables. Each table may have its own unique identifier, making it easier to reference.
Fields.Comment: N/A

GdlDomainLabel: Clinical Data View about Samples and Biomarkers
GdlDomainDescription: This domain holds data from different biomarker datasets showing patient's demographic information, sample information, biomarker details and more.
